# Bounded Semantic Planning and Deterministic Compilation for Reliable Enterprise Text-to-SQL

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#semantic-path-compilation)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.16663v1) · arXiv:2608.16663v1, 17 August 2026

**Reading coverage:** All 16 PDF pages, sections 1–10, formal contract, route/grain pseudocode, figures 1–2, result/sensitivity tables, threats, code availability and references.

**Additional inspected sources:** [Reference source and release scope](https://github.com/yai333/Semantic-Planning-and-Deterministic-for-Text-to-SQL)

## Research question

Enterprise SQL can execute while choosing the wrong role, relationship path or aggregation grain.

## Method

The planner selects question-specific governed semantic identifiers and opaque route handles. Deterministic components review plans, lower roles/grain and compile SQL; known violations block release, while undecidable checker findings do not. One fresh retry is permitted after refusal.

## Evaluation

One insurance domain compares SPC with DDL-only generation on 38 adjudicated questions, three runs each, with an all-44 sensitivity. LLM judging handles unsettled cases; supersets count as success in the main rule. The six-item exclusion registry was created after inspecting outputs.

## What the results support

The reported system has more questions correct on all three runs and fewer adjudicated wrong-but-executed outcomes. Strict-equivalence and all-item sensitivities retain the direction. Targeted multiplicity counterfactuals expose known fan-trap defects.

## Limits and qualifications

The compiler was developed on this benchmark; semantic knowledge, retry allowance and possibly sampling differ between arms. Judging is not independently human-validated. Public code excludes evaluation databases, verdicts and exact campaign state, preventing full reproduction. Deterministic compilation does not guarantee a correct business interpretation.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

A bounded architecture case study, useful for separating reproducible relational construction from uncertain semantic selection.
